world_serpent.imported_event: Thor and Yormungander's single shared late-S2 displacement is delivered. Source clash and departure real; no second opening, second serpent or newly arrived older version.
world_serpent.worldscale: The serpent occupies real length and volume. His movement, body contact, breathing/surfacing, attempts to coil, dive, uncoil or cross waterways can affect multiple maritime zones. If truly extended around globe in-scene, its actual mapped spans must be consistent with shorelines, bathymetry, shipping corridors and the time needed to move; do not conveniently compress/re-expand for scene blocking.
world_serpent.dynamic_individual: He is an intelligent Giant-souled character with personal responses to Thor, new waters, frightened crews, weapons, food/territory and possible interpreters; not a friendly transport mount, generic roar-machine, controllable nation-killing spell, infinite poison leak or universal antagonist. He may decline contact, hold a course, spare/defend an actual vessel, react to being attacked or alter passage on purpose.
first_physical_consequences: Ships encounter real portions of his body, wake, dangerous proximity, loss of visibility, displaced water or blocked approaches, determined by actual movement and location rather than magic tides.
Mariners choose whether to turn back, warn others, exploit salvage, demand escort or attempt attack. Track actual survival, vessel losses and reachable coastal response.
A harbor operator's real closure or diversion affects identifiable cargo, price, contract, food or troop passage, not instant worldwide trade shutdown.

More distant consequences can follow interconnected maritime routes, changed ports, witnessed physical events, refugees, commercial networks and actual message delays. A region needn't have personally seen him to experience a lost shipment or changed prices.
